Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure is caused by an overflow in BitInputStream.readBits when reading in LITTLE_ENDIAN mode as the internal bit-cache approaches the maximum usable size of a long.

Evidence and reasoning:
- The implementation sets MAXIMUM_CACHE_SIZE to 63 (bits in long minus the sign bit). See MAXIMUM_CACHE_SIZE = 63.
- In readBits(int) the loop keeps pulling bytes until bitsCachedSize >= count:
  - For LITTLE_ENDIAN it executes: bitsCached |= (nextByte << bitsCachedSize); then increments bitsCachedSize by 8.
- There is even a comment hinting at the danger (around where the code is returned): “bitsCachedSize >= 57 and left-shifting it 8 bits would cause an overflow” — but there is no code handling this situation.
- The problem: when bitsCachedSize is already large (>= 56) and another byte is added, nextByte << bitsCachedSize shifts an 8-bit value by 56 or more. This either:
  - pushes bits into the sign bit (bit 63), which the code is supposed to avoid (hence MAX = 63), or
  - discards bits outright when the shift exceeds the 64-bit width.
  In both cases, the internal cache silently overflows/corrupts.
- The loop can also set bitsCachedSize to 64 (by unconditionally adding 8) even though the code intends to keep at most 63 usable bits. This breaks the invariant that the sign bit must remain unused and results in masked/shifted outputs being wrong later.
- The failing test littleEndianWithOverflow expects a correct 12-bit value (1186 = 0x4A2), but because an earlier iteration of the loop overflowed the cache while accumulating bytes to satisfy a large read, the cache content became corrupted. When the test then extracts 12 bits, it gets an incorrect value.

Why this matches the test and bug report:
- The current issue explicitly mentions an overflow in BitInputStream.readBits.
- The test name littleEndianWithOverflow and its expected pattern (commented as 01001010-0010, i.e., 0x4A2) indicate it is verifying correct bit assembly in little-endian mode across a boundary where the cache would have been near capacity.
- The code’s LITTLE_ENDIAN branch does not protect against exceeding MAXIMUM_CACHE_SIZE during accumulation; it lacks the necessary pre-flush or chunked assembly to avoid pushing into the sign bit or shifting beyond the width.

Root cause:
- BitInputStream.readBits(int) does not guard against overflowing the internal long cache when accumulating additional bytes in LITTLE_ENDIAN mode. Specifically, it allows bitsCachedSize to grow past the safe threshold and performs nextByte << bitsCachedSize with bitsCachedSize >= 56, causing loss or corruption of bits and, consequently, wrong values returned by subsequent reads.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
